stem: An online marketplace's checkout flow calls several downstream services, and the operations team needs to know exactly which one of those downstream calls is adding the most latency to a single slow checkout request.

choices.text: Configure a CloudWatch alarm that triggers when a resource's latency metric crosses a threshold
Search aggregated application logs with CloudWatch Logs Insights for the affected time window
Add a custom CloudWatch dashboard widget showing latency per service
Enable AWS X-Ray tracing to build a service map and trace the request across the downstream calls

rationale: AWS X-Ray traces a single request across multiple services, builds a service map, and pinpoints which specific downstream call in that chain introduced the latency, which is exactly the per-request, which-call-is-slow question the operations team is asking. A CloudWatch alarm reports that a metric crossed a threshold on a resource; it can say that latency rose overall, but it cannot identify which downstream call within one request caused it. Searching aggregated logs with CloudWatch Logs Insights can surface patterns across many log entries, but it does not trace a single request's path through multiple services the way distributed tracing does, so pinpointing the one slow call in the chain is much harder. A custom CloudWatch dashboard widget only visualizes metrics that are already being collected per service; it does not trace an individual request across service boundaries to attribute the added latency to one specific downstream call.
